To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the UL131-UL128 genes of HCMV are essential for the infection of endothelial, epithelium and myeloid cell types, that they are complexed with gL and gH to form a pentameric complex, that the immune response to HCMV is mostly directed to the PC and that the PC represents a potentially protective HCV vaccine.

1) the UL128L locus is essential for leuko-tropism and for the ability of the virus to transfer from endothelial cells to leukocytes; 2) the UL128 locus encodes the pentameric gH/gL/UL128/UL130/UL131A complex; and 3) the humoral immune response to PC is the most protective against HCMV.
the HCMV UL128L is essential for virus dissemination and that anti-HCMV antibody responses to PC are protective.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of HCMV tropism and dissemination, the role of the immune system in controlling virus spread, and the development of a HCMV vaccine.
the identification of the HCM V PC as a major determinant of cell tropism, dissemination, virus-induced immunosuppression and vaccine development.
the identification of the molecular basis of HCMV cell tropism, the characterization of the immune response to PC and the development of an HCMV vaccine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PC is essential for HCMV cell tropism, dissemination, immune response, and vaccine development.
ULb' is the HCMV gene locus that encodes the PC.
the UL128L gene is a major determinant of HCMV cell tropism and virus transfer to circulating leukocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the UL131- 128 locus is a key region of the HCV genome, as it encodes for a protein complex (PC), whose role is to facilitate virus dissemination in the host and to elicit a strong immune response, which is a prerequisite for vaccine development.

the PC is essential for virus dissemination in the host, for virus transfer from infected endothelial and epithelial cells to leukocytes, and for induction of the humoral immune response, thus being an attractive vaccine target.
the PC is a key component for the virus to disseminate from the infected endothelial cell to the leukocyte and to the fetus, and is a target for the immune system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PC, a complex of five proteins, is the key to HCMV cell tropism and virus dissemination.

wild-type HCMVs are not only genetically diverse but are also phenotypically different from their laboratory-adapted counterparts, thus emphasizing the importance of using wild-type HCMVS in research and clinical practice.

, although the UL128L locus was identified by chance and the pentameric protein complex was identified by chance, the whole field of HCMV biology was changed by the identification of this complex and the subsequent studies of its role in HCMV pathogenesis and immunity.
